Prose:
The guard’s staff remained grounded against the stone floor, a silent promise that violence had paused but not ended. Caelen kept his posture slumped, letting his broad hands rest loosely at his sides to reinforce the image of a confused, harmless asset. He focused on breathing slowly, ensuring he didn’t exhaust himself with unnecessary movement. His collar pressed cold against his throat, a constant reminder of his new reality.

Across the pen, the masked man in purple flipped another page of his ledger, the black tip of his cane tapping rhythmically like a metronome marking out time for humiliation. The scarred captive slumped further into the shadows near the overturned crate, his defeat absolute and unquestioned. Caelen watched without judgment; power here was fragile, held together by the overseer’s will and the guards’ fear of disobedience.

He scanned the pen again, eyes adjusting to the gloom. The thirty captives huddled in clusters, some wrapped in rags, others bare-chested with skin stained by soot or dried blood. A few pairs of eyes met his briefly before looking away, wary but unwilling to make a connection. On the far side, the young woman who had been struck was being helped up by another captive, her trembling hands clutching a small bundle she clung to protectively. There were alliances forming here, fragile and fleeting, built on mutual survival. He would play along with whatever role they wanted him to fill.

Caelen adjusted his stance slightly, testing the limits of his restraints again, feeling the rough texture of the rope burn against his skin. Outside the gate, the patrol moved in its predictable rhythm, boots crunching on gravel that seemed too loud for how little dust there was. Inside, the air smelled of wet stone, unwashed bodies, and something metallic—blood, rust, or fear. He didn’t try to name it. He just breathed, waited, and prepared to endure whatever came next.
